t: AirSim: What AirSim Is: The Drone's Simulator
title: AirSim: What AirSim Is: The Drone's Simulator
description: AirSim is the open-source simulator built for AI: Unreal Engine visuals, a purpose-built physics engine for multicopters (and cars), and Python/C++ APIs that let learning algorithms fly thousands of missions. It exposes the vehicle's state, camera, lidar, and controls as clean APIs — the drone as a programmable object. The community continuation keeps it alive for research after Microsoft's archive. For drone AI, it is the training ground.

title: AirSim: APIs: Flying with Code
description: AirSim's APIs are the interface: takeoff, moveToPosition, getImages, getLidarData — the vehicle reduced to function calls. AI researchers script missions, collect datasets, and close learning loops without touching a radio. The API's determinism (fixed-steppable, seedable) makes experiments reproducible. Learning to 'fly' in AirSim means learning to command precisely and read state completely.

t: AirSim: Physics: The Custom Flight Model
title: AirSim: Physics: The Custom Flight Model
description: AirSim's physics engine was written for drones: rigid-body dynamics with motor models, drag, ground effect, and wind — fast enough for real-time and accurate enough for control development. It is not a general robotics engine; it is a drone engine, and the specialization shows in the flight feel. The parameters (mass, inertia, motor curves) are the modeling decisions, measured where it matters.

title: AirSim: Sensors: Cameras, Lidar, Depth
description: AirSim's sensors serve AI: cameras with configurable resolution and FOV, depth cameras, lidar with point clouds, plus ground-truth segmentation. The data feeds perception training and testing directly. Noise models keep the data honest; the ground truth keeps the scoring automatic. For drone vision — obstacle avoidance, landing-site detection, tracking — this is the data factory.

t: AirSim: Your First Flight: Scripted Takeoff
title: AirSim: Your First Flight: Scripted Takeoff
description: The hello-world: connect, confirm the sim, arm, takeoff to 5 meters, hover, land — ten lines of Python. The vehicle obeys; the APIs report. From there: waypoint squares, image capture loops, lidar scans. The beginner's real lesson is the API's completeness — if you can think it, you can script it, and the script is the experiment.

t: AirSim: HIL: Real Autopilot, Simulated World
title: AirSim: HIL: Real Autopilot, Simulated World
description: AirSim's HIL configuration closes the loop with real hardware: a Pixhawk running PX4 or ArduPilot receives simulated sensor data and returns actuator commands to the sim. This tests the actual flight stack — the binary that will fly — against scenarios too risky for the field. HIL is where 'the sim says' meets 'the hardware does', and discrepancies are gold: they reveal modeling gaps before the field does.
key_facts: Tests the binary that will fly

t: AirSim: AI Training: Learning to Fly
title: AirSim: AI Training: Learning to Fly
description: AirSim is built for learning: reinforcement learning trains obstacle avoidance and landing policies across thousands of episodes; imitation learning clones expert trajectories; the APIs reset the world instantly for the next episode. The sim-to-real gap is the research frontier — domain randomization and careful physics narrow it. Policies graduate from sim to caged flight to open flight, each stage gated on the previous.
key_facts: RL and imitation learning at scale

t: AirSim: Defensive Uses: Rehearsing Without Risk
title: AirSim: Defensive Uses: Rehearsing Without Risk
description: AirSim's defensive value is rehearsal: search patterns over synthetic terrain, perimeter patrol routes, and emergency procedures practiced thousands of times before the real aircraft launches. Operators train against the sim; autonomy proves itself in the sim. The field then validates the rehearsal, not the idea — the idea was settled in the thousand runs.

t: AirSim: Recording Datasets: The Data Pipeline
title: AirSim: Recording Datasets: The Data Pipeline
description: AirSim's recording pipeline captures images, depth, lidar, and vehicle state to disk in organized logs — the raw material for perception datasets and imitation learning. The discipline is the recording manifest: which sensors, which rates, which scenario seed — so the dataset is reproducible and its gaps are known. Recorded well, one afternoon of scripted flights becomes a dataset that trains models for months.

title: AirSim: Environments: Building the World
description: AirSim runs in Unreal environments — city blocks, rural terrain, custom maps — and the environment is the experiment's context. Building worlds in Unreal (or using the bundled ones) with the right fidelity for the question is the craft: perception questions need visual richness; control questions need accurate physics and wind. Match the world's fidelity to the question asked.

title: AirSim: Debugging: The Sim-to-Real Gap
description: AirSim debugging often means gap-hunting: the policy works in sim and wobbles in reality — so compare: motor response curves, sensor latencies, wind models. The tools are system identification (measure the real vehicle's responses) and ablation (change one sim parameter, re-test). The gap is never fully closed; it is managed, measured, and respected.
key_facts: System identification of the real vehicle

t: AirSim: Timing: The HIL Loop Budget
title: AirSim: Timing: The HIL Loop Budget
description: HIL lives or dies on timing: sensor data to the autopilot, actuator commands back, all within the real-time budget — typically a few milliseconds per loop. Jitter in the sim-to-hardware path looks like sensor noise to the autopilot and can destabilize control. The measurement is loop-time histograms on the real link; the fix is usually prioritized threads and locked clocks.

title: AirSim: Testing: Scenario Matrices
description: Mature AirSim practice runs matrices: scenarios × seeds × conditions, with pass/fail on mission success and safety events. The matrix is the test suite; its results gate deployment. Flaky scenarios are fixed or removed — a flaky test teaches nothing. The matrix grows with field lessons: every surprise becomes a scenario.

title: AirSim: Real-World Pattern: Search-Training Program
description: A complete pattern: a search team trains its drone AI in AirSim — synthetic terrain with randomized victims, weather, and lighting — across 50,000 episodes, then validates in caged flight, then field exercises. The sim supplied the rare cases (night, rain, obscured victims) the field could never schedule. When the real call comes, the AI has seen it ten thousand times.
